asof: Settles Fri 23 Oct 2026 · written Sun 25 Oct
headline: The SOFR strip prices a Fed that hikes to about 4.6%; the Street sees one more hike. Fade 2027, keep December.
summary: SR3 contracts closed Friday 4–5bp higher in implied rate across 2027–28 as Brent's jump to $116.72 and a 59.8 PMI prices-paid gauge revived inflation worries, but the month still belongs to the bulls: 2027 contracts are 20–27bp lower in rate since 30 September as weak jobs data and Thursday's AI-driven haven bid pulled hike pricing back. The strip now implies 3-month SOFR rising from 3.90% to a 4.61% peak in the Sep 2027 quarter (SR3U7), about 70bp above today's fixing, with a shallow 13bp of easing priced over 2028–29. That is more tightening than economists expect: all 100 in the latest Reuters poll see a December hike, but around 60% put the peak at 4.00–4.25%, one hike away.
drivers: Oil keeps the front end honest

Gulf attacks and Hormuz tanker strikes put Brent at its highest settle since April; with core PCE running about 3.1% and the PMI's prices-charged index at a 2022 high, the market will not price out December, which holds near 20–22bp (around 80–85%).
October's rally came from growth, not inflation

Softer jobs data and Thursday's 17bp drop in 2-year yields on AI concerns did most of the work; hikes priced by March 2027 fell from 63bp at the end of September to 44bp, so the 2027 contracts led the month's gains.
Funding is tight at the margin

SOFR has printed 3.87–3.90%, 0–2bp over EFFR, with reverse repo usage near zero and the 99th percentile near 3.98%. Month-end and Treasury coupon settlements can push fixings up, which matters for the front contract (SR3U6) whose quarter is now one-third fixed.

With Chair Warsh avoiding forward guidance, Wednesday's FOMC (2.5bp priced) is unlikely to validate a path beyond December, leaving 2027 pricing to the data: two payroll reports and the CPI that lands the day after the December meeting.
spreads: The hiking path lives in the whites: U6/Z6 +24.5bp and Z6/H7 +23bp each price roughly one full hike, H7/M7 +15bp about 0.6 of one, and the curve flattens to M7/U7 +5bp before turning negative from U7/Z7 (−1bp). Month to date the whites have flattened sharply (Z6/H7 −8.5bp, Z6/Z7 −15.6bp, now +42bp) as 2027 hikes were taken out faster than December's. Beyond the peak the reds and greens show only −1.5 to −2.5bp per quarter of easing, so the Z7/Z8 spread at −8bp implies just a third of a cut over 2028. The H7/M7/U7 fly at +10bp marks M7 as the kink where the market stops adding hikes.
fed: Fed funds futures and the SOFR strip tell the same story within 2–3bp: about 10% odds of an October hike, 21.5bp cumulative by December (about 76% P(hike)), 44bp by March, 61bp by June and a 68.5bp peak at the September 2027 FOMC, implied EFFR 4.57%. At the 16 Oct settle December was 26.5bp and March 52bp; at end-September, 31bp and 63bp. Consensus (Reuters, ING) is one hike in December to 4.00–4.25%, then a long pause; the Fed's own median also stops after one more move. The market is therefore carrying about 45–50bp of 2027 tightening that neither the Fed's projections nor the median economist expects.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Z6's quarter (16 Dec–17 Mar) mostly captures the December hike the Street is certain of, while M7 carries the roughly 1.5 extra 2027 hikes that consensus and the Fed's median do not. If December is delivered and guidance stays absent, M7 should rally relative to Z6. The spread has already narrowed 13bp this month, so momentum is on the trade's side.
ideas.risk: A second leg of the oil shock or a hot core PCE/CPI forces the market to price a faster cycle; the spread sat between about 40bp and 51bp for most of the four weeks before Thursday's rally.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: If the core view is wrong and the Fed does take SOFR to 4.6%+ into a $100+ oil shock, the easing that follows is likely to be bigger than the third of a cut now priced for 2028. This leg profits when the peak is pushed higher or growth cracks, so it offsets the core trade's main risk. Use about half the size of the core trade.
ideas.risk: A 'higher for longer' plateau through 2028 with no cuts, which would leave the spread flat to positive.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract into month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: About a third of U6's quarter is fixed near 3.88–3.90%, and an October hike is only about 10% priced, so the upside is small while month-end and coupon-settlement funding spikes in SOFR can only cost a long. Revisit after the 28 Oct FOMC.
ideas.risk: A surprise October hike would cost U6 roughly 10bp (half its quarter would reset 25bp higher); a dovish surprise would lift it only a few bp.

watch: A weak tail would lift Z6/H7 and challenge the core trade.
Hold expected (2.5bp priced); hawkish dissents from Hammack, Kashkari or Logan would firm December.
A print at or above 3.95% signals reserve scarcity and pressures U6/Z6.
Fiscal outlook and term premium; mostly a red/green contract story.
A second soft report would extend October's 2027 rally; a strong one revives 2027 hikes.
The main risk to fading 2027 hikes; watch $120 as a pain point for the core trade.
